input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: Reusing the wrapper's statistics dictionary makes overlapping invocations overwrite each other's active statistics. The same change also removes invocation isolation in the synchronous wrapper.
- rationale: Start invocation A, let its first attempt fail and enter a retry sleep, then run invocation B of the same decorated function successfully before A resumes. B clears and initializes the dictionary that A's retry object also uses, resetting attempt_number to 1. When A succeeds on its second attempt, its statistics incorrectly report one attempt; callbacks inspecting A's retry object also see B's statistics. Previously each invocation's copy retained its own dictionary.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism: the wrapper's single statistics dict is cleared and reused across overlapping invocations, so B's clear/initialization wipes A's attempt_number and A reads mixed statistics. It covers both the async and sync wrappers, as the label does.
